q: What is the main difference between a standard view and a metric view?
o: A metric view is always materialized
A metric view fixes the measure definition, while the grouping is chosen at query time
A metric view can only be queried from dashboards
A metric view does not support joins
e: A standard view fixes both aggregation and GROUP BY. A metric view stores only the definitions, and the engine computes the measure correctly at whatever grain the query asks for.

q: A view stores unique_customers per month. Why is SUM(unique_customers) over a year wrong?
o: SUM is not allowed on views
Distinct counts are not additive: the same customer is counted in many months
Because of NULL values
It is correct
e: COUNT(DISTINCT) is non-additive. A metric view recomputes it from detail rows for the requested grain.

q: Which query against a metric view is valid?
o: `SELECT * FROM sales_metrics`
`SELECT region, SUM(net_revenue) FROM sales_metrics GROUP BY region`
`SELECT region, MEASURE(net_revenue) FROM sales_metrics GROUP BY region`
`SELECT m.*, c.name FROM sales_metrics m JOIN customers c ON ...`
e: Measures must be wrapped in MEASURE(). SELECT * and direct joins are not allowed (use a CTE for joins).

q: Which agent metadata property does Genie import automatically to match user wording to fields and measures?
o: format
synonyms
display_name
materialization
e: Synonyms (up to 10 per field or measure) are imported by Genie automatically. Formats and display names are mainly used by dashboards and BI tools.

q: You prototyped KPIs as a local metric view in an AI/BI dashboard. How do you make them available to a Genie Agent?
o: Copy the dashboard
Use 'Export as a metric view' to create a Unity Catalog metric view
Genie can read local metric views directly
It is not possible
e: Local metric views are scoped to one dashboard. Exporting creates a governed UC metric view that Genie, SQL and BI tools can use.
